stem.en: How are mitochondria and chloroplasts alike, and how are they different?

text.en: Both make food in sunlight, but only mitochondria have two membranes around them.

feedback.en: Only chloroplasts make food, and both of them have two membranes.

text.en: Both have two membranes and their own DNA, but they do different jobs.

feedback.en: Yes. Chloroplasts make food in sunlight, and mitochondria release energy from food.

text.en: Both are found only in plant cells, and both of them store starch for later use.

feedback.en: Animal cells have mitochondria too, so both are not found only in plant cells.

text.en: Both release energy from food, but only the chloroplasts have their own DNA.

feedback.en: Chloroplasts make food. Both organelles have their own DNA.

explanation.en: Mitochondria and chloroplasts each have two membranes, their own DNA and their own ribosomes. A mitochondrion has cristae and releases energy from food, in plant and animal cells. A chloroplast has discs with chlorophyll and makes food in sunlight, in plant cells.

hints.en: Which one makes food, and which one releases energy from it?
